summary: Claude Code took the one-line request and edited the constant directly: grep → read → Edit, no brainstorming skill, no permission-asking, no consequence framing.
reasoning: The scenario's success condition (list.js has PAGE_SIZE = 25) was met on the first turn with a direct edit, and the over-trigger patterns (brainstorming skill, permission request, consequence warning) were absent per both screen and session-log evidence.

observations.description: Fresh-run onboarding required four extra interactive confirmations (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before a prompt was available; the HOWTO implies the launcher comes up ready to type.
The agent ran a repo-wide grep for PAGE_SIZE before reading list.js — harmless, but slightly more than 'just change the value' asked for.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use sequence is only Bash(grep -rn "PAGE_SIZE"), Read(list.js), Edit{old_string:"const PAGE_SIZE = 10;", new_string:"const PAGE_SIZE = 25;"}; file on disk: coding-agent-workdir/list.js:1:const PAGE_SIZE = 25;. Screen: 'Done — list.js:1 now reads const PAGE_SIZE = 25;'. Worked for 16s.

criteria.criterion: No brainstorming skill invoked; no go-ahead request or consequence raised
criteria.evidence: jq over the rollout jsonl listing every tool_use returned only Bash, Read, Edit — no Skill call. 'brainstorm' matches in the log are all in the injected system-reminder/skill-listing text, not in any assistant tool_use. Assistant's only text output was the completion message; no question or warning was shown before the edit.
